turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (CLINICAL_STAFF): He'll be with you in a minute. The computer out here is after freezing, so don't be surprised if he asks you to say things twice. Have a seat.
[SEG0002] person_2 (PATIENT): You're grand. I was half afraid I'd be left out here till lunch. I did two laps of the car park before I found a spot, and the rain is desperate.
[SEG0003] person_3 (DOCTOR): Come on in. One second, the screen's gone blank again. Right. What can I do for you?
[SEG0004] person_2 (PATIENT): It's this big toe. Fierce sore and swollen, came on last night. I didn't sleep a wink, and the dog thought it was gas, jumping on the bed every time I turned.
[SEG0005] person_3 (DOCTOR): Sorry, say that again, which toe? It jumped to the wrong chart.
[SEG0006] person_2 (PATIENT): The right big toe. The pain is desperate, even the sheet on it is too much, and it's swelled up something shocking.
[SEG0007] person_3 (DOCTOR): Started last night, not before that?
[SEG0008] person_2 (PATIENT): Last night, yeah. I went to bed grand after the match, not a bother on me all day. I was out the back looking at the roses yesterday, if you can believe that.
[SEG0009] person_3 (DOCTOR): Any knock or injury to it?
[SEG0010] person_2 (PATIENT): No, nothing like that. Sure I was only sitting in the chair watching the telly.
[SEG0011] person_3 (DOCTOR): Any fever or shivers? And is the skin broken, that you can see?
[SEG0012] person_2 (PATIENT): No fever, and I'm not shivery. The skin isn't broken, it's just red and puffy. My wife called it a little tomato at seven this morning, which I didn't love.
[SEG0013] person_3 (DOCTOR): Has the same thing happened before?

[SEG0014] person_2 (PATIENT): The same yoke, about a year back. Or it might be longer, I couldn't give you the date. They did a uric acid that time and your woman said it was borderline. I never kept the letter.
[SEG0015] person_3 (DOCTOR): Hold on, frozen again. The blood test, say that once more for me.
[SEG0016] person_2 (PATIENT): Uric acid, about a year ago, and they told me borderline. No number that I remember. The toe settled after a few days that time. I only rested it.
[SEG0017] person_3 (DOCTOR): Any tablets? A water tablet in particular?
[SEG0018] person_2 (PATIENT): Yeah, the water one, for the blood pressure. Every morning. My brother Mick is on something like it and he never shuts up about his salt.
[SEG0019] person_3 (DOCTOR): The name and the dose, please. Sorry, say it again, I clicked the wrong box.
[SEG0020] person_2 (PATIENT): Bendroflumethiazide. 2.5 milligrams, once a day, by mouth. Small ones from the chemist.
[SEG0021] person_3 (DOCTOR): What about drink? Beer?

[SEG0022] person_2 (PATIENT): Weekends, mostly. A few pints of a Saturday with the lads if the club match is on. I don't bother Monday to Friday, the wife would have my head. We were in the pub last Saturday and the chat went on far too long.

[SEG0023] person_2 (PATIENT): Oh, here, I'm after remembering. I did give it a kick. In the night I got up for a cup of tea and I caught the right big toe off the leg of the chair. A proper smack. It wasn't even sore straight after, so I went back to bed.
[SEG0024] person_3 (DOCTOR): You told me there was no injury. So it was the right big toe, off the chair, last night?
[SEG0025] person_2 (PATIENT): It was, yeah. Sorry. It only came back to me there. Same toe that's killing me now.
[SEG0026] person_3 (DOCTOR): Sock off, so. It's hot, red and swollen over the big toe joint. The other toes are grand, and there's no break in the skin.

[SEG0027] person_3 (DOCTOR): I'll think out loud for a second. Pain that comes on overnight, beer at the weekend, a water tablet, and the same thing a year back with a borderline uric acid, that is most likely gout. You did kick the chair though, so a plain injury is still possible, and I am not calling it definite gout.

[SEG0028] person_2 (PATIENT): Gout. My uncle had that and he was a martyr to it. Do I have to knock the pints on the head for good? There's a wedding in three weeks and I'm not being the fella stuck on the minerals.

[SEG0029] person_3 (DOCTOR): Not for good, but lay off it while this is hot. I'll start colchicine, five hundred micrograms by mouth twice a day for three days, for the toe. Stop it if the diarrhoea starts.
[SEG0030] person_2 (PATIENT): Is that hard on the stomach? The lad next door swears by naproxen for his knee, those anti-inflammatory ones. Would that not be easier?

[SEG0031] person_3 (DOCTOR): If the colchicine doesn't suit you we can switch to naproxen, 500 milligrams by mouth twice a day with food. Not the two together. We'll start the colchicine and leave the naproxen unless we need it.
[SEG0032] person_2 (PATIENT): Grand. Half a milligram twice a day, three days. I'll stick a note on the fridge or I'll forget, same way I forget the keys.

[SEG0033] person_3 (DOCTOR): I also want a blood uric acid today. Just that. It can come back normal in the middle of an attack, so we'll see what it says and I won't hang the diagnosis on the number.
[SEG0034] person_1 (CLINICAL_STAFF): Sorry for sticking my head in. If it's the uric acid I can send him downstairs, they've a slot before twelve.
[SEG0035] person_3 (DOCTOR): Yes, book the serum uric acid. And book him back to me in a week to go through it.

[SEG0036] person_2 (PATIENT): A week is fine. Do I keep the water tablet? The clutch is the left foot so I was thinking about the drive home, then I remembered the accelerator is the right one. I'll manage, I'm sure.

[SEG0037] person_3 (DOCTOR): Keep the bendroflumethiazide going as usual, don't stop it yourself. Rest the foot up today. And if you get a fever or the redness starts spreading, come back sooner, don't wait the week.
[SEG0038] person_2 (PATIENT): Sound. I'll tell herself to leave the good blanket off the bed. Thanks a million, and sorry for the car park speech earlier.
[SEG0039] person_1 (CLINICAL_STAFF): Come out to the desk and I'll put the blood test and the week visit in the book.

features: doctor_thinks_aloud: the doctor lists possible causes or says what they will not conclude yet. Only record a clinical assessment if the doctor actually states a leading or differential impression; 'let's see what the tests say' is not an assessment.
test_result_recalled: the patient reports an old test or result ('they said it was borderline'); recorded as reported history/investigation only as far as said, not as a confirmed value.

omissions.text: The patient said the toe pain was so bad he did not sleep at all last night.

The patient initially denied any knock or injury to the toe, then later remembered and clarified that he had kicked the right big toe off the leg of a chair during the night; this contradiction/history change was discussed explicitly.
The patient said the kicked toe was not sore immediately after the injury and he went back to bed.
Examination: the other toes were normal/intact ('grand'). The recorded fact says 'Other toes abnormal' with status absent, which is wrong wording.
The doctor stated he was not calling this definite gout.
Naproxen was discussed as an alternative because the patient asked whether colchicine is hard on the stomach and suggested naproxen; this preference/concern is not recorded.
The doctor specified the uric acid test as a serum uric acid and said it should be done today/downstairs before twelve.
The doctor explained that uric acid can be normal during an acute attack and he would not rely on that number alone to make the diagnosis.
